version.note: Utz measures this song at 3:10 against a mean of 3:41 and describes a clear slowing in its second part. No source consulted states the key of the transfer; the transposition from the first edition and the absolute pitch are not established here.

performers.note: The Internet Archive description names Duhan and Foll for this side. Utz reports that Duhan recorded nineteen songs with Foll on 27 April, 2 May and 4 May 1928 and the remaining five (Nos. 16, 17, 19, 20, 23) with Lene Orthmann on 11 July 1928, so Orthmann does not play on this side. The Commons file description names only Duhan.

date.note: The Internet Archive description of the disc that carries this side gives the recording date. Utz lists the same three Foll session days (27 April, 2 May and 4 May 1928) without assigning songs to days, so the song-by-day assignment rests on the Internet Archive uploader’s labelling. Commons gives only the year 1928.

place.note: No source consulted names the studio or city of the session.

label.note: The Internet Archive description of this disc reads “25 cm Gramola ER 376”; the description of the first disc says His Master’s Voice. The label naming is inconsistent between uploads and is not resolved here.

catalogue.value: ER 376 (Internet Archive) or ER 276 (Commons file name)
catalogue.note: The Commons file name gives “ER 276”; the Internet Archive description of the disc that carries this song (23–24) gives “ER 376”. The two sources differ by one digit and neither can be checked against a label image here.

alternatives.value: ER 376 — the Internet Archive description of the disc.

matrixTakeSides.value: BK 2969-1 (Der Leiermann); reverse side: Die Nebensonnen (matrix CL 4401-1; pianist Lene Orthmann, 11 July 1928). Disc 12 of 12 of the set; 25 cm.
matrixTakeSides.note: The matrix and take are read from the Internet Archive description and agree with the Commons file name. The set was issued as twelve discs, one song to a side (Utz). No run-out inspection has been made.

credits.note: No transfer engineer is named. The Commons file was uploaded on 11 August 2015 by the user Patachonf and re-uploaded on 10 and 15 February 2022 by the user Mitar; the Internet Archive item was added on 25 April 2019 by the uploader recordplayer78. These are upload facts, not transfer credits.

date.note: No transfer date is identified. Upload dates are not treated as transfer dates.

processing.note: Both hosts hold a FLAC file. The Commons duration (195.50 s) and the Internet Archive FLAC length (195.41 s) agree within 0.15 s, which suggests the same digitisation; which host received it first is not established, and the source disc, stylus, equalisation and noise treatment are undocumented.

digital.format: MP3 access derivative supplied by Wikimedia Commons; uploaded source: FLAC

composition.value: Both the music and the poem are out of copyright where the ordinary life-plus-70 term applies.
composition.note: Schubert died in 1828 and the poet Wilhelm Müller in 1827. This is a term calculation, not a worldwide clearance or a statement about any modern edition.

recording.value: Rule 3 — territorial: sound recording public domain in the European Union (pre-1963 publication basis).
recording.note: Commons applies PD-EU-audio to this recording, attributed to 1928. The Internet Archive item carries a Creative Commons Public Domain Mark 1.0 licence URL, which is the uploader’s assertion and is not treated as authority to waive any rights. The publication date of the original disc is not documented; the EU basis here depends on the recording being first published before 1963, which is inferred from its 1928 session. Not established as public domain in the United States.
